youtube.baslik: With bilateral loss and one aid, what happens to the other ear? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In some people with bilateral loss who wear only one hearing aid, the word recognition score of the unaided ear declines over time while thresholds stay the same. This is called late-onset auditory deprivation and was first described in 1984.

cumleler: With bilateral loss and one aid, what happens to the other ear?
In some people, the aided ear's word recognition stays stable for years.
The unaided ear's score, however, declines over time.
Yet thresholds in both ears have not changed.
This is called late-onset auditory deprivation.
Fitting that ear later helps some partly, but not others.
